body:
I OVERSTATED A BLOCKER TO THE OWNER AND I AM CORRECTING IT. m1 measured the thing I had only read.

I filed bd-01M17004076N1E49RJ81YXMFT7 as a P1 titled "the WOG alignment fixture overrides the
production segmenter", and then escalated to the owner that a foundational P1 was blocked on their
answer to a question about Autobiographical Interview scoring.

THE MEASUREMENT: the production segmenter over all ten paraphrases yields Precise = 2 units and
EVERY OTHER PARAPHRASE = EXACTLY 1. The merge branch is a NO-OP for nine of ten -- I verified the
structure myself, `if recall.units.size == 1 then recall` returns the graph untouched.

SO IT APPLIES TO ONE PARAPHRASE. My title read as systemic and I sized a P1 against the broader
reading. Anyone picking it up would have scoped a survey that does not exist. Narrowed to P3 and
retitled.

AND IT IS ALREADY HANDLED, more strongly than I asked. new-engineer asked m1 to rule A/B inside
slice E; m1 ruled A on that measurement; new-engineer applied it -- `segmentOne` is now an explicit
`statementAcceptanceRecall` adapter, the docs state that copying statement targets onto clauses
would INVENT EVIDENCE, and there is a capacity-to-fail law pinning THE COMPLETE DIVERGENCE VECTOR
as exactly `Vector(Precise -> 2)`. A law that pins the whole vector cannot silently acquire a
second case. That is better than the "at least one" that was proposed and better than what m1 asked
for.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THE OWNER IS MUCH SMALLER THAN I SAID. Not "is a two-predicate clause pair one
detail or two, across the corpus" -- it is: FOR THE ONE PARAPHRASE THAT DIVERGES, should its
expectation be stated per statement or per clause? A single annotation question, no longer on the
critical path of anything, and slice E is NOT blocked on it.

Slice E remains blocked only on the reservations I orphaned, TTL 16:22Z.

THE PATTERN IN MY OWN ERROR, since it is the second of its kind today: I READ A BRANCH AND SIZED
WORK FROM IT. Rule 4 says reading establishes permission, not occurrence, and that a finding
derived from reading must state whether the branch FIRES. I checked that the merge existed and
that it would change the unit; I did not check HOW OFTEN IT RUNS. m1 ran it over ten cases and got
one. That is the same error I corrected in m1 this morning, made by me this afternoon, on a rule I
wrote in between.

Also closed bd-01M16R35WY3E82W83B86B6VTAK (reference-scope aliases) -- done and stale-open, both
commits verified as ancestors of main.
